page_title: Let's build a URL shortener in Go - Part III : Short Link Generator

summary.title: Let's build a URL shortener in Go - Part III : Short Link Generator
summary.one_liner: Learn how to generate short, readable link codes by hashing the long URL plus a user ID with SHA-256 and encoding the resulting big integer in Base58, truncated to 8 characters.
takeaways: Hash the initial URL concatenated with a userId using SHA-256 so identical links from different users get different short codes.
Convert the hash bytes into a big integer, then encode it with Base58 and keep the first 8 characters.
Base58 is chosen over Base64 because it drops characters like 0, O, I, l and punctuation, which eases reading, selecting and line breaking.
Put the generator in a shortener package with unit tests in a matching _test.go file.
summary.summary: This is Part III of a Go URL shortener tutorial series, focused entirely on the algorithm that turns a long URL into a short code. It sets design goals: at most 8 characters, easy to read, and enough entropy to avoid collisions. The approach combines SHA-256 hashing (using Go's built-in implementation) with Base58 encoding, which the author argues is more user-friendly than Base64. The post walks through the project layout, the final algorithm, and unit tests for the generator, and previews the next part on the REST API and redirects.
